tools.name: generateHyperExecuteYAML
tools.title: Generate HyperExecute YAML
tools.description:
Generates a HyperExecute YAML configuration for running tests on LambdaTest's HyperExecute platform.

REQUIRED fields: project (language, framework) and testing (testDiscovery.command, testRunnerCommand)
All other fields are OPTIONAL.

Supports multiple languages and frameworks:
- JavaScript/TypeScript: Playwright, Cypress, WebDriverIO, Puppeteer, Taiko
- Python: Pytest, Behave, Robot Framework
- Java: TestNG, JUnit, Cucumber
- Ruby: RSpec, Capybara
- C#: NUnit, xUnit, MSTest
- Mobile (ONLY use appTesting for these): XCUI (iOS), Espresso (Android), Appium

Features:
- Smart framework defaults for common configurations
- Input validation with security checks
- Caching and artifact upload configuration
- Git integration via sourcePayload
- Mobile app testing support (via optional appTesting field)

The appTesting field applies to mobile app testing only; web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, etc.) leaves it out.

testDiscovery.description: How HyperExecute finds the tests to run

command.description: Command to discover tests (e.g., find tests -name '*.spec.ts')

type.description: How tests are discovered: raw runs the command as given, automatic lets HyperExecute detect them

mode.description: dynamic discovers tests on the runner at run time; static uses the list found before the run

testRunnerCommand.description: Command to run tests. Use $test placeholder for test identifier.

concurrency.description: Number of tests run in parallel

autosplit.description: Spread the discovered tests across the parallel runners automatically

maxRetries.description: Retries per failed test when retryOnFailure is on

preCommands.description: Commands to run before tests (e.g., npm install)

language.description: Runtime to install on the runner, e.g. node, python, java

appTesting.description: Mobile app testing configuration (XCUI, Espresso or Appium). Web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, etc.) leaves it out.

framework.description: Mobile testing framework (required if appTesting is used)

appPath.description: Path to app file or lt:// URL

devices.description: Target devices (required if appTesting is used, e.g., 'iPhone 14 Pro-17')

video.description: Record a video of each test

sourcePayload.description: Git integration: fetches the test code from a remote Git repository. Only needed when the code is not already present locally; local code (the usual case) leaves it out.

platform.description: Source platform; git is the only supported value

accessToken.description: Reference to an environment variable that holds the Git token, e.g. ${GIT_TOKEN}; never the token itself

uploadPaths.description: Paths on the runner to upload as job artifacts, e.g. reports/ or screenshots/

mergeArtifacts.description: Merge the artifacts from all parallel runners into one set

type.description: Report FORMAT (not framework name). Use 'xml' for most frameworks (Playwright, Cypress, pytest, TestNG, JUnit generate XML reports). Use 'json' for Cucumber/BDD. Valid: html, json, xml, zip

tools.name: getAccessibilityReport
tools.title: Get Accessibility Report
tools.description: Runs an accessibility scan on the given URLs and returns the issues found. Pass urls to start a scan, or testId to re-read a scan that already ran; exactly one of the two. Results arrive in issueDetails: allIssues (most-severe-first, one page at a time), rules (name and reference link per rule id, listed once), pages (every scanned page with its score and issue count), failedRules (per-rule totals for the whole scan) and pagination. Each issue carries its own howToFix and criteria, measured for that element - two issues sharing a rule can have different causes and fixes. While pagination.nextOffset is not null the results are incomplete: call again with the testId from the response plus that offset, keeping the same filters, until it is null. Page with testId, never by passing urls again - that starts a new scan, costs another run, and can return a different set of issues whose offsets do not line up. a11yReportLink is the dashboard URL and needs a login; shareableLink is public and is only returned by the original scan.

items.description: URL to analyze for accessibility issues

urls.description: List of URLs to scan. Starts a new scan. Provide either urls or testId, not both.

testId.description: Re-read an existing scan by its testId (as returned in a previous response) instead of running a new one. Use this to page through results with offset.

severity.description: Only return issues of this impact level. Omit to get all severities.

pageUrl.description: Only return issues found on this scanned page. Must exactly match one of the URLs in issueDetails.pages.

limit.description: Maximum issues to return in this response (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Index to start from within the filtered, severity-sorted issue list. Pass the nextOffset from a previous response, together with that response's testId, to page through results.

include_rules.description: Return the full rule catalog (about 11 KB) instead of the default ruleCatalog summary of counts per category and disabled rule ids.

tools.name: getAccessibilityReport
tools.title: Get Accessibility Report
tools.description: Runs an accessibility scan on the given URLs and returns the issues found. Pass urls to start a scan, or testId to re-read a scan that already ran; exactly one of the two. Results arrive in issueDetails: allIssues (most-severe-first, one page at a time), rules (name and reference link per rule id, listed once), pages (every scanned page with its score and issue count), failedRules (per-rule totals for the whole scan) and pagination. Each issue carries its own howToFix and criteria, measured for that element - two issues sharing a rule can have different causes and fixes. While pagination.nextOffset is not null the results are incomplete: call again with the testId from the response plus that offset, keeping the same filters, until it is null. Page with testId, never by passing urls again - that starts a new scan, costs another run, and can return a different set of issues whose offsets do not line up. a11yReportLink is the dashboard URL and needs a login; shareableLink is public and is only returned by the original scan.

testId.description: Re-read an existing scan by its testId (as returned in a previous response) instead of running a new one. Use this to page through results with offset.

pageUrl.description: Only return issues found on this scanned page. Must exactly match one of the URLs in issueDetails.pages.

limit.description: Maximum issues to return in this response (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Index to start from within the filtered, severity-sorted issue list. Pass the nextOffset from a previous response, together with that response's testId, to page through results.

tools.name: tm_generate_test_cases
tools.title: Generate Test Cases with AI
tools.description: Generate structured test cases from a requirement or prompt using the Test Manager AI generator (applies the project's Memory Layer — Project & Org Instructions — automatically) and file them into the chosen folder. Requirement documents, specs, spreadsheets or screenshots can be attached via files to ground the generation. Volume = test_scenario_limit × per_scenario_test_cases_limit, capped at 50 per call. By default all generated cases are saved into the folder (one sub-folder per scenario); pass auto_save=false to review before saving. The call returns FAST with a request_id (and a browser progress URL) — generation takes ~30-90s in the background; call this tool again with just request_id to check progress, fetch results, or save. Note: consumes AI generation credits.

project_id.description: Project ID (ULID). Required when starting a new generation.

Each item carries the file name and its raw bytes base64-encoded in content_base64. Supported: .pdf, .docx, .txt, .csv, .xlsx, .json, .xml, .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .bmp, .webp; max 5 files, 10 MB each. Large files are better uploaded in the Test Manager UI, since the base64 content travels in the request. Only used when starting a new generation.

name.description: File name with extension, e.g. requirements.pdf

outcome.description: Expected result, shown as the step Outcome in the UI. Use this key: any other step key (such as expected_result) is rejected.

tools.name: tm_create_test_run
tools.title: Create Test Run
tools.description: Create a test run from chosen test cases — manual (default) or KaneAI (run_type: "kaneai"). Each included test case becomes a TEST RUN INSTANCE — the executable copy of that test inside the run, which carries its own status, remarks and exactly one Configuration. The cases must match the run type: KaneAI runs only take KaneAI-authored cases with completed code generation; manual runs only take manual cases. Optionally attach existing milestones, file into a run folder, and apply a Configuration to all instances (KaneAI configurations must be compatible with each case's platform — web/mobile-app/mobile-browser and iOS/Android).

run_type.description: Run type (default manual). "kaneai" creates a KaneAI run: only KaneAI-authored test cases can be included, and configurations must be kane-supported and platform-compatible.

is_sequential.description: KaneAI runs only: execute the instances sequentially (default false).

milestone_ids.description: Existing milestone ids to attach the run to

folder_id.description: Test-run folder to file the run into

configuration_id.description: Apply ONE Configuration to every included test case (the configuration's top-level id from tm_list_configurations)

configuration_ids.description: Apply MULTIPLE Configurations: each included test case gets one test run instance per configuration (case × configuration), like the UI's Add Configuration checkboxes

assignee.description: Assign every created instance to this organization member: email, username, or user id. Omit to leave the instances unassigned.

tools.name: tm_update_test_run
tools.title: Update Test Run
tools.description: Update an open test run — overall status (Passed / Failed / Skipped / In Progress), title, objective, milestones, folder, add test cases (each added case becomes a new test run instance; cases must match the run's type — KaneAI or manual), apply a Configuration to the run's instances (configuration_id; on KaneAI runs it must be kane-supported and platform-compatible with the targeted cases), toggle sequential execution (KaneAI runs), or archive it. Only open (active) runs can be updated; a closed/archived run returns a clear message. Adding cases/milestones appends, never replaces.

status.description: Set the run's OVERALL status (independent of per-instance results). Manual runs only — KaneAI run status is managed by KaneAI executions.

is_sequential.description: KaneAI runs only: execute the instances sequentially.

add_test_case_ids.description: Test case ids to add to the run (appended)

configuration_id.description: Set ONE Configuration on the run's instances (the configuration's top-level id from tm_list_configurations; each instance carries exactly one configuration)

configuration_ids.description: APPEND multiple Configurations: each targeted test case gets an additional instance per configuration (case × configuration, like the UI); existing configured instances are untouched

assignee.description: Assign the run's instances to this organization member: email, username, or user id ("none" clears). Scope with apply_to_test_case_ids. Omit to keep the current assignee.

apply_to_test_case_ids.description: With configuration_id or configuration_ids: only apply to these test cases (default: all instances in the run)

tools.name: tm_record_test_results
tools.title: Record Test Results (Bulk)
tools.description: Record execution results on a MANUAL run's TEST RUN INSTANCES (the per-run copies of each test case) — max 500 per request, all-or-nothing (larger requests are rejected with nothing recorded). Manual runs only: KaneAI run results are recorded by KaneAI executions, so manual entry on a KaneAI run is rejected. Target an instance by instance_id, or just pass test_case_id and the instance is resolved automatically. Valid statuses: Passed, Failed, Skipped, Not Started (terminal — run-level "In Progress" is set via tm_update_test_run). Re-recording a step status replaces its result: an omitted step remark is cleared; response echoes per-step outcomes. Optional remarks and assignee per result, and per-step results via steps[] (mark individual test steps / BDD scenario rows Passed/Failed/Skipped with remarks, like the UI's per-step Mark Status). Note: this sets INSTANCE statuses; the run's overall status is set separately via tm_update_test_run.

test_case_id.description: Alternative to instance_id: the test case ULID

status.description: Passed, Failed, Skipped or Not Started (instance results are terminal — "In Progress" applies only to the run's overall status via tm_update_test_run)

assignee.description: Assign this instance to an organization member (email, username, or user id; "none" clears). Omit to keep the current assignee.

steps.description: Optional per-step results: mark individual test steps (or BDD scenario rows) of this instance, like the UI's per-step Mark Status

step.description: Step number (1-based, in the order shown on the case/instance)

status.description: Passed, Failed or Skipped

tools.name: smartui_baseline_manage

flags.description:
Generates a HyperExecute YAML configuration for running tests on LambdaTest's HyperExecute platform.

REQUIRED fields: project (language, framework) and testing (testDiscovery.command, testRunnerCommand)
All other fields are OPTIONAL.

Supports multiple languages and frameworks:
- JavaScript/TypeScript: Playwright, Cypress, WebDriverIO, Puppeteer, Taiko
- Python: Pytest, Behave, Robot Framework
- Java: TestNG, JUnit, Cucumber
- Ruby: RSpec, Capybara
- C#: NUnit, xUnit, MSTest
- Mobile (ONLY use appTesting for these): XCUI (iOS), Espresso (Android), Appium

Features:
- Smart framework defaults for common configurations
- Input validation with security checks
- Caching and artifact upload configuration
- Git integration via sourcePayload
- Mobile app testing support (via optional appTesting field)

The appTesting field applies to mobile app testing only; web automation (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, etc.) leaves it out.
